title: Visiting researcher
industry: Microeconomics (JEL D), International Economics (JEL F), Public Economics & Economic Policy (JEL H), Economics, Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics (JEL E), Economics and Social Sciences, Financial Economics (JEL G), Labor and Demographic Economics (JEL J), Econometrics, Statistics and Quantitative Methods (JEL C), Economic Development, Innovation and Growth (JEL O), Finance, Statistics
text:
Eesti Pank is the central bank of Estonia. Its Research Division provides high-quality research on economic and policy issues relevant to monetary policy discussions in Estonia and the ESCB, and contributes to economic forecasting and financial stability assessment by developing economic models. See our website (http://www.eestipank.ee/en) for additional information on the work of Eesti Pank.
Visiting researchers are expected to undertake research projects that align with the general research interests of Eesti Pank. Preference is given to projects that relate to the current research agenda of the Research Division or offer opportunities for collaboration with economists in the Division.
Research projects will be agreed upon in advance. Visiting researchers are expected to present their work at Eesti Pank seminars and actively participate in internal research discussions. They will receive compensation in accordance with Eesti Pank’s remuneration system.
Applicants should have a proven research record and strong written and oral communication skills in English. They should hold a PhD in Economics or Finance. Final-year PhD students are also encouraged to apply.
Visiting researcher appointments typically last between two and four months. The duration of the stay is flexible but should be sufficient to allow for the successful completion of the agreed research project.
Preferred research topics:
Proposals in all areas of economics relevant to central banks will be considered, but priority will be given to research projects on the following topics:
Monetary economics
Financial stability
Household financial behaviour
Real estate economics
Working in the Research Division of Eesti Pank gives applicants the opportunity to:
Gain experience in applied economic research while working alongside Eesti Pank economists
Participate in the economic policy-making process
Attend Eesti Pank seminars and internal research discussions
Gain first-hand insight into the operations and research activities of a Eurosystem central bank
To apply
Applications should be submitted in English and should include:
A cover letter indicating the preferred starting date and duration of the research project
A research proposal, including:The research topic and main research question(s)
A brief literature review
A description of the research methodology and the data to be used

The applicant’s CV
A letter of recommendation (required only for PhD candidates and recent PhD graduates)
A sample research paper, if available
The deadline for applications is 13 December 2026. 
Applications should be sent to Eesti Pank by email to liina.kulu@eestipank.ee (Ms Liina Kulu, Research Division, Economics and Research Department, Eesti Pank).
